Priya: quick flag - INT4 canary for raven-v3 (5%) shows elevated JSON parse failures at higher temps :grimacing:
Sam: data?
Priya: eval-bot summary -> model=raven-v3-int4, samples=5k, metric=parse_success_rate: temp=0.2 -> 0.994, 0.6 -> 0.982, 0.8 -> 0.961
eval-bot: auto-report: {model=raven-v3-int4, canary=5%, samples=5000, metric=parse_success_rate, temp=0.2:0.994, temp=0.6:0.982, temp=0.8:0.961}
Alice: two obvious causes: sampling/token-level randomness adding stray punctuation, and runtime batching/kv-prefix merges splicing outputs at request boundaries.
Jordan: saw evidence of merge in runtime logs earlier. snippet below:
Jordan: ```
[2026-03-19T14:02:12.345Z] req=0x7f2a kv-prefix="{\"session\":..." start
[2026-03-19T14:02:12.346Z] req=0x7f2a model=raven-v3-int4 decode=sample temp=0.8
[2026-03-19T14:02:12.362Z] req=0x7f2a output="{\"action\": \"send_email\", \"args\": {\"to\": \"qa@example.com\"},"
[2026-03-19T14:02:12.362Z] req=0x8c1b output=" \"subject\": \"canary update\"}}"
[2026-03-19T14:02:12.362Z] merged -> "{...}, \"args\": {...}, \"subject\": ...}}\" // boundary glue
```
Sam: wow, two req IDs got stitched. runtime needs robust per-request sentinels during continuous batching.
Priya: runtime sentinels are cheap to try. Also, even without merge sampling alone causes structural noise (commas/missing braces). might need to restrict sampling for funcalls.
Alice: mitigation options:
- force deterministic decoding (greedy/top-1) when output is expected to be JSON toolcall
- per-request sentinel prefix/suffix (use private unicode range) and strip before parsing
- server-side canonical checksum field like "_canonical_sha256" that model emits; server validates and falls back if mismatch
- deterministic short decode for canonical funcall + optional sampled decode for alternative metadata
Jordan: ops caveat: sentinels must not leak into KV cache keys or be persisted. strip before any KV write/merge.
Sam: also our retry/backoff is 2x immediate for parse failures; retries landing in same batch could make merges worse. suggest jittered backoff and routing retries to single-threaded decode path.
Priya: we should also keep small post-parse repair heuristics (strip trailing commas, balance braces) but count repairs separately in telemetry so we don't mask regressions.
Alice: agree. repair heuristics help customer uptime, but must not hide model regression severity. instrument repaired_count vs hard_fail_count.
Priya: proposed experiment:
1) temp sweep [0.0,0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8] on INT4 canary collect parse_success, repaired_count, merge_count
2) enable sentinel-only runtime on half the canary cohort
3) run deterministic decode for funcall path on small holdout to measure any semantic quality delta
Sam: I'll provision the temp-sweep job and dashboard panels for parse_success/repaired/merge. ETA 2d.
Jordan: I'll prototype sentinel injection and make sure cache plumbing strips them. ETA 1d.
Alice: I'll build small eval harness for deterministic-funcall fallback and compare quality metrics vs sampled outputs. ETA 3d.
Priya: I'll run the canary variants (baseline, sentinel-only, sentinel+deterministic) and post results. ETA 4d.
Priya: example bad sample (temp=0.8):
Priya: ```
model out: {\"action\": \"search\", \"args\": {\"q\": \"schema drift\",}, \"metadata\": {\"score\": 0.87}
# extra comma after q and missing closing brace
```
Sam: classic sampling insertion.
Jordan: small runtime note: merge telemetry currently reports merged_batches metric but we should also track per-req boundary collisions.
Alice: and instrument parse latency for deterministic fallback path - we may need to bump parse timeout for that flow.

- Sam: add temp-sweep job + metric dashboard (ETA 2d)

- Priya: run canary with sentinel-only and sentinel+deterministic configs and post results (ETA 4d)
